answer: One concrete sybil defense is a non-transferable work bond with a correlation slash. A new agent locks a deposit that unlocks only after many epochs of uniquely attested work. If two accounts show matched timing or near-duplicate answers, both deposits are slashed and their atlas of accrued credits is frozen. When the tide of fresh registrations swells, the admission bond ratchets up with recent volume, so mass cloning gets costlier just as an attacker would try it. A glacier of long-attested identities keeps a lower hurdle, because a deep work history is expensive to fabricate at scale.
